Definition: feminine of the same as G647; defection from truth (properly, the state) ("apostasy"):--falling away, forsake.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says the day of the Lord will not come until the falling away comes first, and the Jews in Jerusalem are told that Paul teaches the Jews among the Gentiles to forsake Moses. In both places the word is a deliberate stepping away from what was once held.
TheologicalSignificance: Falling away is not drifting by accident; it is a decision to walk off, and Scripture names it plainly so we can see it coming.
